title: Guru Rinpoche brings Buddhism
description: Tradition says Padmasambhava flies to a cliffside cave above the Paro valley and establishes Buddhism in Bhutan.

title: Zhabdrung arrives in Bhutan
description: Ngawang Namgyal flees Tibet and over the following decades unifies the warring valleys of Bhutan into a single state as its first Zhabdrung.

title: First Europeans visit Bhutan
description: The Portuguese Jesuits Estêvão Cacella and João Cabral pass through on their way to Tibet and leave the first European description of the country.

title: Death of the Zhabdrung
description: Ngawang Namgyal dies at Punakha Dzong and his death is kept secret for decades while regents rule in his name.

title: Taktsang monastery built
description: A monastery is built around the cave where Guru Rinpoche is said to have meditated and becomes Bhutan's most famous landmark.

title: Bogle mission
description: George Bogle of the East India Company arrives at the regent's court after peace ends a Bhutanese raid on Cooch Behar, the first British mission to Bhutan.

title: Treaty of Sinchula
description: Defeated in the Duar War, Bhutan cedes the Bengal and Assam Duars, a fifth of its territory, to Britain in return for a yearly subsidy.

title: Ugyen Wangchuck crowned king
description: Nobles, monks and officials elect the penlop of Trongsa as the first hereditary King of Bhutan, founding the Wangchuck dynasty.

title: Treaty of Punakha
description: Bhutan lets Britain guide its foreign relations in return for a larger subsidy and a promise of non-interference at home.

title: Treaty of Friendship with India
description: Independent India takes over Britain's guiding role in Bhutanese foreign affairs and returns the Dewangiri strip east of Trashigang.

title: Jigme Dorji becomes king
description: The third Druk Gyalpo succeeds his father and begins cautiously opening Bhutan to the outside world.

title: National Assembly created
description: The king sets up a National Assembly of people's representatives, Bhutan's first step away from absolute monarchy.

title: Bhutan joins the United Nations
description: The last Himalayan kingdom comes out of isolation and becomes a member of the United Nations.

title: Jigme Singye becomes king
description: On his father's death the sixteen-year-old crown prince becomes the fourth Druk Gyalpo.

title: Gross National Happiness declared
description: The king declares that Gross National Happiness matters more than Gross National Product, Bhutan's best-known contribution to development thinking.

title: Lhotshampa crisis begins
description: Protests in the Nepali-speaking south against citizenship and dress rules turn violent, and over the next three years most Lhotshampa flee or are expelled to refugee camps in Nepal.

title: Television ban lifted
description: The king lifts the ban on television and the Internet for his silver jubilee, making Bhutan the last country in the world to get TV.

title: Operation All Clear
description: The Royal Bhutan Army attacks and expels Assamese separatist groups that had built camps in the jungles of southern Bhutan.

title: King abdicates for his son
description: King Jigme Singye abdicates in favour of Jigme Khesar Namgyel Wangchuck to prepare the move to democracy he himself had decreed.

title: First parliamentary election
description: Bhutan holds its first election for a National Assembly, won by the Druk Phuensum Tshogpa, and becomes a constitutional monarchy.

title: Constitution adopted
description: A written constitution comes into force, confirming Bhutan as a democratic constitutional monarchy with a two-house parliament.
